_readme: InoxTv Ad Manager (AdX) remote config — ONE file, both apps.
Host at: https://jitendrasoftwaredeveloper.github.io/inoxtv-config/inoxtv-adx.json
THIS IS A SECOND AD SOURCE, NOT A REPLACEMENT. inoxtv-admob.json still owns everything about
AdMob; this file only decides whether the app asks Google Ad Manager first.
PRIORITY: Ad Manager wins when it fills. AdMob is requested ONLY when Ad Manager misses on that
slot. While Ad Manager is serving a placement, that slot's AdMob unit is not requested at all.
A slot therefore holds ONE source at a time — see FALLBACK below.
preroll.json is a DIFFERENT file and belongs to the IMA / VAST / VMAP live-TV path.
Nothing in this file touches it, reads it, or can affect an IMA ad.
SWITCHES — the same four levels, with the SAME KEY NAMES, as inoxtv-admob.json, so the two files
read the same way. Each file's switches control ONLY its own source:
1. master_enabled ............... false = no Ad Manager ad anywhere, both apps. AdMob carries on.
2. debug_ads_enabled ............ false = no Ad Manager ad in DEBUG builds, both apps
3. <platform>.master_enabled ... false = Ad Manager off for that one app, the other keeps going
4. slots.<name>.enabled ........ false = that one placement never asks Ad Manager
A slot key the app asks for but this file does not contain behaves exactly like enabled:false.
AD MANAGER OFF IS NOT ADS OFF. It means AdMob, exactly as before. The two masters are
independent, so the combinations are:
this false + admob true ... AdMob only — byte-for-byte the app as it was before this file
this true  + admob true ... Ad Manager first, AdMob on a miss — the goal
this true  + admob false .. AdX only — AdMob silenced, Ad Manager still serving
both false ................ no ads at all
To stop EVERY ad you must edit BOTH files. There is deliberately no single kill switch; if one
is ever wanted it should be added then, not assumed now.
THIS FILE HOLDS EXACTLY WHAT THE APP ASKS FOR — the same 9 mobile slot keys and 1 TV slot key as
inoxtv-admob.json, one for one, plus the fallback numbers. A key the code does not read does
NOTHING: it is parsed, stored and never looked up. New placement = code first, then a key here.
WHAT THE CODE ACTUALLY READS. Everything else here is documentation for whoever edits the file:
top level ..... master_enabled, debug_ads_enabled, allow_test_units_in_release, fallback
per platform .. master_enabled, slots
per slot ...... enabled, path, test
NOT read ...... version, updated, network_code, adx_publisher_id, admob_publisher_id,
name, format, _note, _readme
Unknown keys are ignored and missing keys take their defaults, so this file can gain keys
later without breaking an app already installed in the field.
EVERY DEFAULT IS THE QUIET ONE. A missing or misspelled enabled reads as false, a missing or
blank path refuses, a missing master_enabled reads as false. A file that loses a key goes quiet,
never loud. Every failure — file absent, unreachable, malformed, network changed, path not of
this network — means the app falls through to AdMob, which is exactly the behaviour of a build
without this feature at all. This file can never break advertising; it can only add a source in
front of it.
TWO ACCEPTED PATH PREFIXES, SPLIT BY FIELD — and which field may name which IS the safeguard:
/22853635592/ ... always accepted, in 'path' AND in 'test', in every build type. Your network.
/21775744923/ ... accepted in 'test' ONLY, never in 'path', in every build type. This is
Google's public DEMO network: unmonetised test ads, nobody's revenue.
So 'path' is checked against your network and against nothing else, and a RELEASE build can
never request inventory outside it — whatever is pasted in, and whatever the flags say.
Demo inventory is reachable in a release build only through the one boolean below.
The demo prefix is still gated, just not by this check: 'test' is only read at all when the
test units are in play — DEBUG build type, or allow_test_units_in_release in a release one.
Refusing demo in 'test' here as well would make that flag a no-op, which is the one thing it
exists to do.
A path failing its own field's check is ignored and AdMob serves. Never widen this to a bare '/':
a mistyped network code would then silently request a stranger's inventory and pay them.
NETWORK CODE IS THE ONLY THING VALIDATED. The app checks exactly one thing about a path: that
it starts with /22853635592/. That number never changes, which is what makes it safe to compile
into the app as a constant.
network code ........ 22853635592 ............ sits INSIDE every ad unit path, and is the WHOLE
validation. Nothing else about a path is checked.
AdX publisher ID .... pub-5889298706423519 ... shown in Ad Manager (Admin > Global settings).
Exists for app-ads.txt and for your own
reference, nothing else. NOT part of any ad unit
path, so NO CODE COULD CHECK IT even if wanted —
it does not appear in the string.
AdMob publisher ID .. pub-6161953663322185 ... a DIFFERENT number, same company. This is what
ca-app-pub-6161953663322185/... is built from,
validated in inoxtv-admob.json.
So one company holds TWO publisher IDs, one per product, and neither one appears anywhere in this
file's validation. AdMob unit IDs and Ad Manager paths are not interchangeable in any direction.
app-ads.txt — nothing to do with what the app does, recorded because the two IDs above are why it
needs two rows. Google authorises a seller per publisher ID, and a hosted app whose seller ID is
missing stops being monetized. https://inoxtv.com/app-ads.txt was checked on 2026-10-07 and
already carries BOTH:
google.com, pub-6161953663322185, DIRECT, f08c47fec0942fa0
google.com, pub-5889298706423519, DIRECT, f08c47fec0942fa0
f08c47fec0942fa0 is Google's certification authority ID. Nothing to do here.
PATH FORMAT — the same hierarchy the Ad Manager console shows:
/<network_code>/<parent ad unit name>/<ad unit name>
Note the leading slash. A path is NOT an AdMob unit ID (those look like
ca-app-pub-6161953663322185/1130586516). The two must never be swapped between the two files:
each file's validator accepts only its own shape, so a paste into the wrong file is refused
rather than mis-billed. That is the whole reason this is a second file instead of a second
field in the AdMob one.
PATHS BELOW ARE PRE-FILLED, AND MUST BE CONFIRMED BEFORE GOING LIVE. They are derived from the
console names recorded in inoxtv-admob.json plus the parent ad unit you supplied
(Inoxtv-app-Ad-Units). That derivation is not the console's word for it. A wrong path does not
error — it silently never fills, which is the hardest possible thing to notice from inside the
app. Check each one, then set master_enabled true.
TEST vs LIVE, same shape as inoxtv-admob.json — keep BOTH, never overwrite one with the other:
test = Google's DEMO unit for that format. Detached from your account, always fills, safe to
click, no invalid-traffic risk.
path = the live Ad Manager path. Paste it in; leave test where it is.
Overwriting test with path means a debug build can never show an Ad Manager ad again.
BANNERS: the demo unit has to match the SHAPE OF THE REQUEST, which is why every banner slot
here carries fixed-size-banner and not adaptive-banner. A band requests a FIXED AdSize, built
from the window width and the slot's height (MobileBannerPresenter.step), never an anchored
adaptive size — the anchored helper derives the height itself and would take the band's height
away. adaptive-banner is the demo unit for the request this app does NOT make, and a demo unit
asked for the wrong shape comes back as no fill, which reads exactly like Ad Manager being off.
DEBUG BUILDS. debug_ads_enabled true means a debug build serves slots.<name>.test — Google's
demo units — so Ad Manager is testable with no console work and no invalid traffic. Set it false
and Ad Manager is off in debug entirely. Either way a debug build NEVER reaches your live paths:
the resolver returns test whenever BuildConfig.DEBUG, before path is even looked at.
To exercise YOUR yield groups rather than Google's demo ads, put your real path in test AND
register the device as a test device via RequestConfiguration.setTestDeviceIds — the ID is
printed in logcat on the first ad request, and emulators count automatically. Beware: mediated
ads carry NO 'Test Ad' label, so a network's ad on a test device looks exactly like a real
one. Put each network in test mode, or simply do not click.
allow_test_units_in_release: true = RELEASE builds serve the DEMO paths instead of your real
ones. It reads slots.<name>.test and never touches path, so there is nothing to revert but this
one boolean. Use it ONLY for the R8 / minified-APK check, then set it back to false. Left true
in production it earns exactly ZERO while every ad still displays perfectly — the one key in
this file whose wrong value costs money rather than merely showing nothing.
FALLBACK — a slot holds ONE source at a time, never two buffers. This costs nothing: the SDK's
preload cache holds six ads app-wide, and holding an AdMob ad while Ad Manager is filling would
spend that budget on an ad that must never be shown.
failures_before_switch: Ad Manager misses in a row before the slot re-points to AdMob. 2 is a
compromise — one wasted request on a dead path, but a single network blip cannot demote the
whole session. Range 1..10; 0, negative, missing and anything above 10 all read as 2, the
default — never as 1, because a bad path and one bad request are told apart by the second
attempt, and that is exactly what this counts.
reprobe_interval_s: how long a slot stays on AdMob before trying Ad Manager again. 1500 = 25
minutes. Clamped to 60..21600 (1 min .. 6 h).
The re-probe is the important one. Fill is a property of COUNTRY and TIME OF DAY, not of the
app: with 100+ countries, Ad Manager will fill in some and not others, and will fill in a
country at 8pm that it ignored at 4am. Without a re-probe, one bad minute pins the session
to AdMob and 'Ad Manager first' quietly stops being true.
This is PER SLOT, not per app. Ad Manager filling player_fullscreen_banner says nothing about
onboarding_banner, and a global switch would demote slots that were working.
CAPS ARE NOT HERE, ON PURPOSE. max_per_session and min_interval_s stay in inoxtv-admob.json,
because they describe the PLACEMENT, not the source, and two files each claiming a cap could
disagree about how many interstitials a session may show. The 90-second gap between full-screen
ads also counts both sources together, through one shared controller — there is no second budget
for the second source.
WHAT ELSE IS DELIBERATELY ABSENT, so that a diff against inoxtv-admob.json is not misread as an
omission. Every key the AdMob file carries is accounted for:
PRESENT here, same meaning .. name, format, enabled, test, _note (path replaces live)
app_id .................... Ad Manager and AdMob share one application ID, and it is compiled
into each host rather than configured in a file.
reward_gates, reward_unlock_hours
these describe the FEATURE GATE, not the ad source: whether a gate
exists, which features it covers, how long an unlock lasts. One
answer for both sources, owned by inoxtv-admob.json — and read from
there whichever source ends up serving, so an unlock earned on an
Ad Manager ad lasts the window set in the AdMob file and vice
versa. This holds even with AdMob switched off entirely and Ad
Manager the only source left: the gate stays on, and it is the
slot's own readiness that decides whether an ad is offered.
Never a paywall either way. If no ad is in hand the gate opens.
min_interval_s, max_per_session
placement caps. See CAPS above — the same argument.
console_refresh_s ......... a value SET IN THE ADMOB CONSOLE and recorded in that file. Ad
Manager sets banner refresh on its own ad units in its own
console, so a number copied here would describe nothing.
phase .................... AdMob rollout staging, recorded in that file. Ad Manager is not
being staged the same way, so copying the value across would
assert a rollout plan that does not exist.
publisher ................ replaced by the more precise network_code plus the two publisher
IDs above, because in Ad Manager those are three different things.
REWARDED. isRewardedReady() means an ad is in hand RIGHT NOW, from whichever source is active.
False means the gate opens and the feature is free — never a re-lock, never a wait. Expect a few
more free unlocks than before while a slot is still warming up on Ad Manager. That is the
designed failure direction, not a bug.
TWO REWARDED UNITS, NOT ONE. mobile.slots.unlock_rew.path and tv.slots.unlock_rew.path are
different inventory, exactly as the AdMob live IDs are. Pasting the same path into both would
mis-attribute every impression. The demo test path is legitimately the same string in both —
only the live paths differ.
APP ID. Ad Manager and AdMob are confirmed to share one application ID here, so nothing in this
file carries it and no initialisation change was needed — the SDK is initialised once, from the
AdMob app ID compiled into each host. Given that the two PUBLISHER IDs turned out to differ, this
is the one claim above worth re-checking if AdX returns no fill on a path you know is live: an
Ad Manager app ID would carry the AdX publisher prefix, not the AdMob one. One line and a
rebuild, not a redesign.
CURRENT STATE (2026-10-07) = READY, PATHS UNCONFIRMED. master_enabled and debug_ads_enabled are
both true, so a debug build can exercise Ad Manager immediately against Google's demo units.
RELEASE builds would use the live paths below, which are DERIVED from the console names recorded
in inoxtv-admob.json rather than copied from the Ad Manager console — confirm them before the
AdX code reaches a release build.
Sequencing, so the two halves are not confused: publishing this file changes nothing on its
own, because no code reads it yet. The paths only start to matter when the AdX code ships.
A wrong path is survivable rather than fatal — Ad Manager misses, the slot falls back to AdMob
— but it costs an extra request on every impression until it is corrected.
New ad units return no fill for a few hours up to ~24h after creation. That is not a bug.

unlock_rew.name: INX_MOB_REW_UNLOCK
unlock_rew._note: The feature gates listed in inoxtv-admob.json's reward_gates. Never a paywall: if this slot goes quiet the gate opens rather than locking the user out.

app_open.name: INX_MOB_APPOPEN_RESUME
app_open._note: Shown on a real return to the foreground only. The when-to-show rules live in the app, not here, and the interval between two app-opens is inoxtv-admob.json's min_interval_s.

fullscreen_exit_int.name: INX_MOB_INT_FULLSCREEN_EXIT
fullscreen_exit_int._note: Leaving a fullscreen player — live TV, movies, shows. max_per_session is in inoxtv-admob.json.

section_switch_int.name: INX_MOB_INT_SECTION_SWITCH
section_switch_int._note: OFF here because the placement itself is off in inoxtv-admob.json, where its max_per_session lives. That file decides whether the placement exists at all; this one only decides whether Ad Manager competes for it. If you enable the placement there, enable it here too or Ad Manager simply will not bid.

livetv_browse_banner.name: INX_MOB_BAN_LIVETV_BROWSE
livetv_browse_banner._note: The live-TV BROWSE band only. Live TV in FULLSCREEN is player_fullscreen_banner. inoxtv-admob.json carries the full screen list.

catalog_browse_banner.name: INX_MOB_BAN_CATALOG_BROWSE
catalog_browse_banner._note: Movies, Shows, Recordings and My List browse bands.

player_fullscreen_banner.name: INX_MOB_BAN_PLAYER_FULLSCREEN
player_fullscreen_banner._note: Every band drawn over a video — live TV in fullscreen, the Movies and Shows fullscreen players, and the recording player. Highest-volume placement in the app.

onboarding_banner.name: INX_MOB_BAN_ONBOARDING
onboarding_banner._note: The whole playlist-setup flow, six screens on one unit.

playlist_processing_banner.name: INX_MOB_BAN_PLAYLIST_PROCESSING
playlist_processing_banner._note: The playlist-processing screen — the longest-dwell screen in the app. This is the path you supplied as the example, so it is the one path here copied from the console rather than derived.

unlock_rew.name: INX_TV_REW_UNLOCK
unlock_rew._note: The ONLY ad the TV app serves, by design. TV has no banner, no app-open and no interstitial, so a banner or interstitial slot added to this section would be parsed and then ignored. CONFIRM THIS PATH: the parent ad unit (Inoxtv-app-Ad-Units) is your mobile example, and TV units may sit under a different parent. A wrong parent passes the network check and silently never fills.
